title: Indefinite 2: -нибудь (Any, Not Yet Chosen)
description: The particle -нибудь (кто-нибудь, что-нибудь, где-нибудь) means 'any one at all, it doesn't matter which.' It lives in questions, requests, commands, the future, and hypotheticals, where the referent is still open.
descriptionRussian: Частица -нибудь (кто-нибудь, что-нибудь, где-нибудь) значит «любой, всё равно какой». Живёт в вопросах, просьбах, командах, будущем и гипотезах, где предмет ещё не определён.
intro: The other particle, and it marks the opposite: a referent nobody has picked yet, where any candidate would do and possibly none exists. It shows up in four predictable places, all of which leave the referent open: questions, requests, the future, and hypotheticals. There is a more formal third particle that means much the same thing and belongs in writing.
rules: Form -нибудь pronouns by gluing -нибудь onto a question word: кто-нибудь, что-нибудь, где-нибудь, когда-нибудь, какой-нибудь. The particle is hyphenated and never changes.
-нибудь marks a referent that is NOT YET FIXED: any candidate at all will do, it does not matter which (possibly none). The speaker is not pointing at a particular one.

-нибудь lives in four contexts where the referent is still open: QUESTIONS (Ты что-нибудь нашёл?), REQUESTS / COMMANDS (Скажи что-нибудь), the FUTURE (Я когда-нибудь вернусь), and HYPOTHETICALS / conditions (Если кто-нибудь придёт...).
Do not use -нибудь for a completed action by a real, particular referent. 'Someone already came' is a fact about a definite person, so it takes -то (Кто-то уже пришёл).
-либо (кто-либо, что-либо) means roughly the same as -нибудь but is more formal and bookish; use -нибудь in everyday speech.
examples: Позови кого-нибудь на помощь. (Call someone for help.) Any person will do; a request.
Дай мне что-нибудь почитать. (Give me something to read.) Anything readable; a request.
Ты где-нибудь видел мои ключи? (Have you seen my keys anywhere?) A question, open place.
Давай поедем куда-нибудь летом. (Let's go somewhere this summer.) An unfixed future plan.
Ты был когда-нибудь в Петербурге? (Have you ever been to Petersburg?) A question about any time.
Если кто-нибудь позвонит, запиши номер. (If anyone calls, write down the number.) A hypothetical.

items.promptEnglish: Have you heard anything about this film?
items.hint: This is a question, and the asker has no particular piece of news in mind. Open referent.
items.explanation: A yes/no question with an open referent (any news at all would count) takes -нибудь: что-нибудь. Что-то would imply you already know a specific thing was heard, which a question does not assume. Ничего would need не and would mean the answer is 'nothing.'

items.promptEnglish: Bring me something to drink, please.
items.hint: A request: any drink at all will do, nothing specific is meant.
items.explanation: A request where any candidate works (water, tea, juice, whatever) is the classic -нибудь slot: что-нибудь. Что-то would name a particular drink the speaker has in mind, which contradicts 'anything to drink.' This is one of the four homes of -нибудь: a request.

items.hint: A future plan; the place is not chosen yet. Any spot will do.
items.explanation: A future plan with no place fixed yet takes -нибудь: где-нибудь (anywhere we end up choosing). Где-то would mean a specific place you already know but cannot name, which clashes with an unsettled plan. The future is one of the four homes of -нибудь.

items.hint: A question about any time at all ('ever?'). The referent (a time) is open.
items.explanation: In a question, 'ever?' (any time at all) is когда-нибудь. Когда-то ('once, at a definite past time') would belong in a statement, not this open question. Никогда means never and needs не. This is the question home of -нибудь.

items.prompt: Если _____ позвонит, скажи, что я перезвоню.
items.promptEnglish: If anyone calls, say I'll call back.
items.hint: A hypothetical 'if' clause; the caller is purely imagined, not real yet.
items.explanation: An 'если' (if) clause sets up a hypothetical: the caller does not exist yet and any caller would trigger the instruction. That is the hypothetical home of -нибудь: кто-нибудь. Кто-то would mean a specific real caller, which a hypothetical condition does not have. Никто needs не.

items.prompt: Дай мне _____ книгу, мне всё равно какую.
items.promptEnglish: Give me some book, I don't care which one.
items.hint: The phrase 'мне всё равно какую' (I don't care which) is the giveaway. Choice is open.
items.explanation: 'Мне всё равно какую' (it doesn't matter which) makes the open, any-candidate reading explicit, so the particle is -нибудь: какую-нибудь. Какую-то would point to a particular book the speaker has in mind, the opposite of 'I don't care which.' (Note: какую is the accusative of какой, agreeing with книгу.)

blanks: Спроси у _____, как пройти к вокзалу. (Ask someone how to get to the station.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: A request / command where any passerby will do takes -нибудь, and the preposition у governs the genitive, so the pronoun core declines to кого: у кого-нибудь. Кого-то would name a specific person already in mind; никого would need не.

errorCorrection.sentence: Летом поедем куда-то отдыхать, всё равно куда.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: In summer let's go somewhere to relax - anywhere at all.
errorCorrection.explanation: This is a plan where any destination would satisfy ('всё равно куда'), so the non-specific -нибудь is correct: куда-нибудь. -то would mean the speaker has one specific place in mind, contradicting 'anywhere at all'. Кое-куда hints at a place the speaker knows but won't name.

errorCorrection.sentence: Позвони кому-то, если вечером понадобится помощь.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Call someone if you need help in the evening.
errorCorrection.explanation: This is a future, hypothetical situation (если понадобится) where any helper would do, so -нибудь is correct: кому-нибудь. -то would point to a specific person the speaker already has in mind, which the open 'if you need help' rules out. Никому would require a negated verb (никому не звони, 'don't call anyone'), reversing the sense. Кого-нибудь is the accusative, but звонить governs the dative, so the form must be кому-нибудь. Future plus condition is a reliable -нибудь cue.

minimalPairs.context: Позови _____, мне нужна помощь. (Any person at all; call whoever you can find.)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Call someone, I need help (anyone at all will do).
minimalPairs.explanation: This is a command where any helper will do and nobody is chosen yet, so the particle is -нибудь: кого-нибудь. Кого-то would mean 'call that specific person,' which contradicts 'anyone at all.' A command with an open referent is the -нибудь home; the verb позвать governs the accusative, so the core declines to кого.

minimalPairs.context: Ты _____ ел сегодня? (A question; have you eaten anything at all?)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Have you eaten anything today? (a question, open referent)
minimalPairs.explanation: A yes/no question with an open referent (any food at all) takes -нибудь: что-нибудь. Что-то in a question would presuppose a particular thing was eaten, which the asker does not assume. Questions are one of the four homes of -нибудь.

reviewVocab.definition: attaches to a question word to mark an open, not-yet-fixed referent: any one at all, it doesn't matter which. Lives in questions, requests, the future, and hypotheticals.
reviewVocab.example: Дай мне что-нибудь почитать — подойдёт любая книга.

reviewVocab.definition: anyone / anything: any candidate will do; no particular person or thing is meant.
ever / someday: an unfixed time, typical of questions ('ever?') and future plans ('someday').
